description:
Read the proof AND file-check state for a file session. Returns a compact view:
- isProofable: whether the session's product/config supports proofing.
- isFileCheckAvailable: whether a file check can run. A file check is a preflight report only (no proof file) and is often available when proofing is not.
- files: [{ fileName, isProofable, isFileCheckAvailable }] per uploaded file.
- proofs: newest-first, each { id, fileName, type, status, approvalStatus, invalid, invalidReason, errors[], warnings[], noReport, createdAt, proofFileUrl, totalPages }.
- checks: newest-first file checks, each { id, fileName, type, status, invalid, errors[], warnings[], noReport, createdAt }.

`id` is the proofId / checkId the create call returned — match on it to find the job you just started (an older proof or check for the same file may still be listed). A proof or check is "ready to report" when status is COMPLETED. `invalid: true` means a later configuration change made it stale and it needs re-running — it is computed server-side; just read it. Checks carry no invalidReason (only one reason is kept per session, chosen for proofs, so it reads wrong for checks), so describe a stale check in your own words. `errors`/`warnings` are the preflight messages shown to the customer (capped for length). `noReport: true` means a COMPLETED proof or check has no preflight report (for example a proof copied from a past order), so its errors and warnings are unknown, not empty: never tell the customer it has no issues. `proofFileUrl` is a signed link to the proof PDF. For each file currently in the session, only the latest proof that is neither invalid nor failed can carry it, and only once that proof is COMPLETED. While a newer proof of that file is still running, or if the file was replaced or removed, there is no link. It stops working within 24 hours of this read, possibly sooner; read again for a fresh one. If you pass it on, use it exactly as returned: never shorten, rebuild, or guess it, or the signature breaks. Use this to suggest a proof (or a file check when not proofable), report issues, answer questions about them, and detect when a config change invalidated a proof or check.

fileSessionId.description: File session ID to read proof and file-check state from.

name: get_file_session_proofs
